purpose: Corrected T^2 selection rules with node-dependent sigma and determinantal response framework.
correction: Step 95 used uniform weight w_i=(1,eps_i) for all nodes. Correct: theta_j = s_A^j alpha + eps_j s_B^j beta, so sigma_j = eps_j s_A^j s_B^j. Anisotropy condition: sigma_i = sigma_j.
gate1_unaffected: The beta=0 subcircle gives |theta_j|=1 on every K_j regardless of pole signs. Gate 1 (no quadratic equivariant K→K map) is unchanged.

determinantal_framework.Q_definition: Q_j = sum_{i: sigma_i=sigma_j} q_{ji} xi_i^2 (anisotropic, sigma-matched only)
determinantal_framework.scale_invariance: With equal scales t and unit norms, t cancels. The equation is scale-free at leading order.
determinantal_framework.why_no_critical_scale: Both P and Q are homogeneous degree 2 in source norms. At equal scales the t^2 cancels from both, leaving a scale-free equation. This is the representation-theoretic reason the Step 92 critical-scale story was impossible.

r0_calibration.calibration_test: On the r=0 KE curve, det(response) = 0 must hold: |sum_i c_{ji}| = |sum_{i: sigma_i=sigma_j} q_{ji}|. This is a sharp check on normalization and transport before any mixed number is believed.
r0_calibration.degeneracy_not_vanishing: The r=0 equation gives degeneracy of the response map (kernel direction exists), NOT vanishing of the response coefficients. Linear subtraction F(mixed) - F(compatible) is therefore invalid; the correct comparison is determinantal.
r0_calibration.source_grounding: OSS (doi:10.4310/jdg/1452002879) places the 4-A1 surface (P1xP1)/Z2 as a boundary point of the compactified KE moduli of degree-4 del Pezzo. Smooth KE metrics with bubble scale t_i → 0 exist along a GH-convergent sequence. Step 67 identifies the all-compatible chirality. At a limiting direction, the all-compatible response is degenerate. No local deformation coordinates or Spotti hypothesis needed for this calibration.

diagonal_balanced_comparison.key_fact: All sigma_j = +1 in diagonal balanced. Every pair contributes anisotropy.
diagonal_balanced_comparison.consequence: Diagonal balanced has strictly MORE anisotropic freedom (6 aniso pairs) than all-compatible (2 aniso pairs). This tilts toward solvability rather than obstruction, contrary to the tacit assumption that mixed patterns are harder.
diagonal_balanced_comparison.P_formula: P_j = c_adj1 + c_adj2 + c_diag (three neighbor terms)
diagonal_balanced_comparison.Q_formula: Q_j = q_adj1 + q_adj2 + q_diag (all three, since all sigma match)

r0_comparison.P_r0: P_j^(r0) = c_adj1 + c_adj2 + c_diag (same terms, different pattern may give different coefficients)
r0_comparison.Q_r0: Q_j^(r0) = q_diag (only diagonal sigma matches in all-compatible)
r0_comparison.additional_aniso_in_mixed: Adjacent Q terms q_adj1, q_adj2 are present in diagonal balanced but absent in all-compatible.
